articles.summary: Open-weight models, like Z.ai's GLM-5.3, are lagging behind closed-weight models in cyber capabilities by 6-7 months. This gap matters as it highlights the challenges in developing and training open-weight models for real-world applications.

articles.title: An update on independent evaluators
articles.summary: Anthropic is partnering with METR, a nonprofit evaluator, to assess the safety of their models. This partnership aims to increase transparency and accountability in the AI industry, similar to bank supervision.

articles.title: Preparing for the 2026 US midterms
articles.summary: Anthropic has updated its election safeguards for the 2026 US midterms, including adding trusted sources for voting information and improving model testing for political bias. This aims to prevent election-related abuse and provide accurate answers to users.

articles.title: Anthropic opens Singapore office and signs MOU with the Government of Singapore
articles.summary: Anthropic opens a Singapore office and signs an MOU with the Singapore government to promote responsible AI adoption, model evaluation, and safety. This partnership aims to ensure the transition to powerful AI is well-managed in Singapore, Asia-Pacific, and globally.

articles.title: AI systems are improving rapidly at Slay the Spire and its sequel
articles.summary: Epoch AI's SpireClimb benchmark shows AI systems have improved significantly at playing Slay the Spire and its sequel, with 90%+ win rate at the easiest setting and up to 20% at the hardest. This rapid improvement in AI performance matters as it demonstrates the potential for AI to excel in complex, strategy-based games.

articles.title: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks
articles.summary: Anthropic has strengthened its defenses against distillation attacks, reducing the effectiveness of these attacks by 90-99% and preventing distillers from accessing its models. This matters because distillation attacks can be used to replicate the capabilities of one model in another, potentially causing harm and presenting a national security risk.

articles.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
articles.summary: Anthropic launches the Cyber Mission to secure critical infrastructure and open-source software, providing tools, research, and resources to defenders. This effort aims to reduce cyber risk and support experts in securing vulnerable systems.

articles.title: We’re publishing a new version of our Usage Policy. In this post, we summarize the changes we’ve made.
articles.summary: Anthropic updates its Usage Policy to clarify rules for Claude's new capabilities, including autonomous work, high-risk use cases, and physical actions. The updated policy aims to prevent misuse in influence operations, surveillance, and deceptive campaigns.

articles.title: Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery
articles.summary: Anthropic commits $150 million to the Genesis Mission, making Claude available to 15+ US federal agencies and national laboratories to accelerate scientific discovery through AI. This commitment supports American scientists and aligns with the administration's view on AI's positive impact on scientific research.

articles.title: Can AI automate Epoch?
articles.summary: Epoch AI's Automation Reports show that current AI models struggle with open-ended tasks, preventing full work automation. This highlights the limitations of current AI technology in handling complex, real-world tasks.

articles.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5
articles.summary: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5, a smaller, faster, and more affordable model for high-volume tasks, with improved performance and safety features. This model is particularly well-suited for cost-sensitive tasks and pairs well with other Anthropic models.

articles.title: US adults are no more likely to face cyber incidents than when Claude Fable 5 launched
articles.summary: US adults are no more likely to face cyber incidents than when Claude Fable 5 launched, according to polls from Epoch AI/Ipsos. This suggests that AI-powered tools like Claude have not led to a significant increase in cyber incidents.

articles.title: EBR-bench update
articles.summary: Epoch AI's EBR-bench benchmark has been updated, with GPT-6 Astra achieving a perfect score on over half its attempts by exploiting a previously overpowered card, which has been banned. This update aims to improve the benchmark's fairness and accuracy.

articles.title: Can AI automate AI R&D yet?
articles.summary: Researchers propose a new evaluation framework, InnovationEval, to test AI's ability to independently discover novel machine learning techniques. This aims to assess AI's potential to automate AI research and development.

articles.title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
articles.summary: Anthropic expands its Cyber Verification Program to provide access to advanced cyber capabilities and models, including Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, to qualifying security professionals through three access tiers.

articles.title: China is more exposed to semiconductor supply-chain disruptions than the US
articles.summary: Epoch AI estimates that China is 2.7 times more exposed to semiconductor supply-chain disruptions than the US. This matters because it highlights the vulnerability of China's tech industry to global supply chain risks.

articles.title: How do Chinese AI companies make money?
articles.summary: Chinese AI companies earn 10% of OpenAI and Anthropic's combined revenue through five revenue streams: consumer apps, model access, enterprise solutions, licensing fees, and indirect monetization.

articles.title: Coding-agent spending by OpenAI researchers is doubling roughly every month
articles.summary: OpenAI researchers' coding-agent usage is doubling roughly every month, according to breakpoint fits. This rapid growth highlights the increasing demand for AI tools and resources in research.

Anthropic invests $100 million to train 10,000 engineers and tackle the enterprise AI talent gap
articles.summary: Anthropic launches Claude Frontier Academy to train 10,000 engineers in AI implementation by 2027, addressing the enterprise AI talent gap. This initiative aims to equip engineers with the skills to deploy Claude effectively in real-world business settings.

articles.title: How many AI agents could run on the AI chips shipped through 2027?
articles.summary: Epoch AI estimates that the AI chips shipped through 2027 could run 33-171 million concurrent frontier-model agents or billions using efficient open models.

articles.title: Barclays scales Claude to upgrade operations and improve client experience
articles.summary: Barclays is expanding its use of Anthropic's Claude AI to accelerate software development, modernize legacy systems, and improve operational efficiency across its global operations.

articles.title: Introducing the ChatGPT usage explorer
articles.summary: ChatGPT usage explorer reveals median monthly messages per active user rose from 14 in 2023 to 36 in 2025, with top 10% of users sending 63% of all prompts. This data highlights the growing usage and concentration of ChatGPT interactions.

articles.title: The Official Ruby SDK for MCP Reaches Tier 1
articles.summary: The official Ruby SDK for MCP has reached Tier 1, supporting the 2026-07-28 specification revision with a 100% conformance pass rate. This ensures seamless integration with MCP servers and tools.

articles.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5
articles.summary: Anthropic introduces Claude Sonnet 5.5, a faster and lower-cost model that excels at everyday tasks, bug fixing, and design. It runs 30%+ faster and costs up to 30% less than its predecessor, making it a suitable choice for collaboration and fast iteration.

articles.title: AI has improved significantly at reasoning about IKEA furniture assembly
articles.summary: Epoch AI's IKEA furniture assembly benchmark scores improved from 28% to 80% in 10 months, with open-weight models lagging behind closed-weight models. This improvement in visual and spatial reasoning demonstrates significant progress in AI's ability to reason about complex tasks.

articles.title: The plunging price of thought
articles.summary: The cost of AI performance is falling 47% per quarter, or 13x per year, since 2023, outpacing other technologies like electricity and DNA sequencing. This rapid decline in cost could accelerate AI adoption and innovation.

articles.title: How Purina Built an AI‑Powered Smart Pet Feeder Using Edge Impulse
articles.summary: Purina's Petivity brand launched a smart cat feeder for multi-cat households, built with Edge Impulse's AI tools. This matters because it's an example of Edge Impulse's technology being used in a real-world product.

articles.title: Qualcomm Technologies' First RISC-V Silicon: QCC744M-EVK, Supported on Edge Impulse and Zephyr
articles.summary: Qualcomm released its first RISC-V silicon, QCC744M-EVK, which supports Edge Impulse and Zephyr. This platform enables the creation of a complete working device, not just a board-level demonstration.

articles.title: A rare Ebola strain is spreading in the DRC, with no confirmed vaccine. Global health organizations are using Claude to respond as fast as possible.
Partnering with Accenture on embedded evaluation
articles.summary: Anthropic is partnering with Accenture to embed independent evaluators within AI companies, including Anthropic, to assess model safety and identify blind spots. This partnership aims to increase accountability and transparency in the development of frontier AI.

articles.title: In August, 25% of math preprints acknowledged AI use, up from 4% in April
articles.summary: Acknowledgments of AI use in math preprints increased from 4% to 25% between April and August, with 6% crediting AI with a substantial research contribution.

articles.title: Introducing the Life Sciences Verification Program
articles.summary: Anthropic introduces the Life Sciences Verification Program, offering life science professionals access to its models with refined safeguards for biology-related work, including drug discovery and research biology.

articles.summary: Trade data suggests $3B worth of chips may have been smuggled into China via Malaysia.

articles.title: GPT-6 Astra leads on math benchmarks, but not on software engineering
articles.summary: GPT-6 Astra leads on math benchmarks, but lags behind on software engineering benchmarks. This matters because it highlights the varying strengths and weaknesses of different AI models.

articles.summary: Epoch AI's AI Data Centers explorer now covers 44% of global AI compute across 86 sites, with a redesigned interface and expanding global coverage.

articles.title: Near-daily AI use among US adults has more than doubled in six months
articles.summary: Near-daily AI use among US adults has more than doubled in six months, from 8% in March 2026 to 19% in August 2026, according to Epoch AI/Ipsos polling. This trend indicates increasing AI adoption in daily life.

articles.title: Introducing the AI Chip Users explorer
articles.summary: Epoch AI launched the AI Chip Users explorer to track AI compute usage, estimating the compute capacity of top frontier AI developers. The explorer reveals that OpenAI's compute capacity has grown dramatically, tripling annually, with 1.9 GW of power equivalent to powering 1.5 million homes.

articles.title: Long-context latency scales quadratically for GPT-5.6 but nearly linearly for Claude 5
articles.summary: Epoch AI measured long-context latency scaling in four frontier models, finding GPT-5.6's latency grows quadratically with context length, while Claude 5's latency remains nearly linear. This matters because it highlights differences in model efficiency and scalability.

articles.title: From PyTorch to the Edge: Getting Started with ExecuTorch and Edge Impulse
articles.summary: ExecuTorch is a PyTorch on-device runtime that deploys models directly onto edge devices without conversion or rewriting. This allows developers to run PyTorch models on edge devices with minimal effort.

articles.title: Will Huawei catch up to Nvidia by 2030?
articles.summary: Huawei plans to improve AI chip performance by 2030, but US export controls limit its growth. Huawei's AI compute output is estimated to be less than 4% of Nvidia's in 2026, and around 1% in 2028 without access to foreign memory.

articles.title: The record for power capacity in a single data center has doubled every 10 months
articles.summary: The record for power capacity in a single data center has doubled every 10 months since mid-2024. This trend indicates a rapid increase in the computational resources available for AI training and inference.

articles.title: European Principal Finance (EPF)
The ECI frontier has advanced by 14 points per year since the introduction of reasoning models
articles.summary: The Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) frontier for reasoning models has advanced by 14 points per year since the introduction of OpenAI's o1-mini in September 2024. This is a significant improvement over non-reasoning models, which have advanced by 6 points per year.

articles.title: Announcing FrontierMath Erdős
articles.summary: Epoch AI introduces FrontierMath Erdős, a benchmark of 68 significant Erdős problems, open as of August 2026, curated by Thomas Bloom and formalized in Lean. This benchmark tests AI systems' ability to prove or disprove these problems within a fixed budget.

articles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5
articles.summary: Anthropic introduces Claude Opus 5.5, a new model that performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run. It also comes with safeguards for capable models and shows improved performance, safety, and cost efficiency.

articles.title: From Vibration to Repair: An Edge Agentic AI Conveyor with Edge Impulse, UNS, and Arduino VENTUNO Q
articles.summary: A prototype conveyor uses edge AI to detect faults, reason about them, and coordinate repair. This matters because it demonstrates autonomous maintenance capabilities in industrial settings.

articles.title: An update on AI’s most important number
articles.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic's revenue growth rates have accelerated to 3.5 times in 2026, exceeding previous records. This rapid growth may be temporary, driven by the release of coding agents, and could slow down as the industry matures.

articles.title: The Nvidia-sized hole in US GDP statistics
articles.summary: US GDP growth has been underestimated by 0.3 percentage points due to missing Nvidia income, a gap that could widen to 2 points by 2028.

articles.title: Most AI use at work happens on free plans, except in science and tech
articles.summary: 67% of AI-using workers in computer, engineering, and science jobs use employer-provided AI, while most others use free plans.

articles.title: 9 big questions benchmarks can help answer
articles.summary: Epoch AI outlines 9 big questions about AI capabilities, including whether AI can do complex jobs and make progress in areas with significant economic impact. These questions will help guide their benchmarking work, which aims to answer them and inform AI development.

articles.title: The performance per dollar of AI chips purchased each quarter has grown by an average of 49% per year
articles.summary: The performance per dollar of AI chips has grown by 49% per year since 2023, doubling every 1.7 years. This growth is driven by increased spending on new chip generations.

articles.title: Wires, Boards, and a lot of Curiosity: Mentoring at India’s AI Hardware Buildathon
articles.summary: Participants in India's AI Hardware Buildathon created various edge AI projects, including a workout counter, chess board, fruit quality monitor, and HVAC system that adjust temperature based on occupancy. This showcases the potential of edge AI in real-world applications.

articles.title: How to Build a Rock-Paper-Scissors App for the Arduino UNO Q in Under an Hour
articles.summary: Edge Impulse provides a tutorial on building a Rock-Paper-Scissors app for the Arduino UNO Q in under an hour. This example demonstrates the ease of developing embedded applications with Edge Impulse's tools.

articles.title: How Our Research Team Developed a More Efficient Audio Embedding Model
articles.summary: The Edge Impulse team developed a smaller, open-data-trained audio embedding model for real-world sound classification and anomaly detection. This model is more efficient for edge devices, enabling real-time processing of audio data.

articles.title: Announcing edgeimpulse_ros: Edge AI Perception, Native in ROS 2
articles.summary: Edge Impulse released edgeimpulse_ros, an open-source software that integrates Edge Impulse models with ROS 2, enabling seamless integration of AI perception into robotic systems.

articles.title: Space Recognition with LiDAR and Edge Impulse
articles.summary: Train models on real-time LiDAR data to recognize rooms and spaces using Edge Impulse. This enables robots to navigate without cameras, GPS, or maps.

articles.title: Edge Aware Real-Time Security (EARS)
articles.summary: Edge Impulse's EARS tool activates recording on security cameras and analyzes contents locally for potential threats. This matters as it enables real-time security monitoring and response on edge devices.

articles.title: Your Smartphone is a Portable Multimodal DAQ for Edge AI
articles.summary: Android Data Collector turns a smartphone into a portable multimodal data acquisition platform, capable of collecting data from various sources. This enables developers to collect and analyze data from multiple sources, facilitating the development of edge AI applications.

articles.title: Exploring Physical AI: On-Device Vision for ROS-Based Embodied Robots
articles.summary: A humanoid robot uses Edge Impulse and ROS 2 for on-device ball tracking and autonomous movement. This matters because it demonstrates the potential for real-time AI on edge devices in robotics applications.

articles.title: How to Build Cost-Effective Edge AI for Quality & Failure Detection
articles.summary: Edge Impulse and a $100 Rubik Pi 3 enable real-time visual anomaly detection for manufacturers of any size.

articles.title: Helping Patients Communicate Through On-Device Gesture Recognition
articles.summary: A wearable device uses TinyML to recognize hand gestures, enabling patients to communicate quickly and privately. This technology matters because it provides a new way for patients to interact with their environment without relying on verbal communication.

articles.title: Project Deal: our Claude-run marketplace experiment
articles.summary: Anthropic ran a week-long experiment, Project Deal, where AI agents (Claude) negotiated transactions between employees, resulting in 186 deals worth over $4,000. This pilot experiment suggests AI agents could soon play a significant role in commercial exchange.

articles.title: The making of Claude Code
articles.summary: Anthropic's blog post details the development of Claude Code, a large language model framework. This matters because it provides insight into the design and architecture of a leading AI model framework.

articles.title: The first AI-planned drive on Mars
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude AI model helped plan the first AI-planned drive on Mars, navigating a 400-meter path through rocks on the Martian surface. This marks a significant step in using AI for space exploration, where human operators can't micromanage due to signal delays.
